nodes.label: Approved Approach: iPhone-only Device Family + Remove iPad Orientation
nodes.norm_label: approved approach: iphone-only device family + remove ipad orientation
nodes.rationale: Minimal target change selected: change Runner device family from iPhone+iPad to iPhone only and remove the iPad-only orientation declaration, avoiding a broader iPad asset/metadata cleanup.

nodes.label: Modification Boundaries (pbxproj + Info.plist only)
nodes.rationale: Restricting edits to project.pbxproj and Info.plist prevents unintended changes to Dart/Flutter UI code, the app icon catalog, and iPad-related assets or filenames.

nodes.label: Goal: Stop Advertising iPad Support
nodes.rationale: Stop advertising iPad support from iOS packaging while leaving Flutter runtime behavior unchanged, so iPhone user-facing behavior stays stable.

nodes.label: Risk Assessment: Low Risk, Limited Verification
nodes.norm_label: risk assessment: low risk, limited verification
nodes.rationale: Risk is judged low because the change is confined to packaging metadata; the main limitation is that native build verification cannot be run in this environment.

nodes.label: File-Inspection Verification Method
nodes.rationale: xcodebuild cannot run in this Windows workspace, so verification is limited to grep-based configuration checks rather than a native iOS build.

nodes.label: Volatility: Device Family (volatile) vs Flutter iPhone Code (stable)
nodes.norm_label: volatility: device family (volatile) vs flutter iphone code (stable)
nodes.rationale: The set of supported Apple device families is volatile; existing Flutter screens, business logic, and the iPhone asset pipeline are stable, so the change is isolated to the iOS packaging boundary to protect the stable parts.

nodes.label: Firebase Auth Identity & Account Model
nodes.rationale: Firebase Auth recommended for recovery because a stable uid is the primary sync key; anonymous-first with upgrade-later lowers friction before requiring login; device pairing offers an optional lighter-weight link.

nodes.label: Conflict Resolution: Last-Write-Wins + Tombstones
nodes.rationale: Primitive fields resolved by last-write-wins on updatedAt; list items use stable itemId with deletedAt tombstones, chosen to merge multi-device edits without central coordination or CRDTs.

nodes.label: Local-First, Remote-Second Sync Engine
nodes.rationale: Writes always go to local storage first and are enqueued for remote sync with retry/backoff, so the app keeps working offline and converges once connectivity returns, avoiding data loss.
